solution: Interpret each matrix as a bipartite graph with five labeled row vertices and five labeled column vertices. Every vertex has degree 2, so the graph is a disjoint union of even cycles. The only possible component sizes, counted on either side of the bipartition, are 5 or 3+2. A single 10-cycle gives 5!·4!/2 = 1440 matrices. For components of sizes 3 and 2, choose the three rows and three columns in C(5,3)² ways; the 6-cycle can be arranged in 3!·2!/2 = 6 ways, and the remaining 4-cycle is unique. This gives 100·6 = 600 matrices. The total is 1440 + 600 = 2040.
insight: The number of alternating cycles on n labeled vertices in each part of a bipartite graph is n!(n−1)!/2 for n ≥ 2.
insight_justification: Fix one vertex in the first part as the starting point. Order the n vertices in the second part and the other n−1 vertices in the first part; each undirected cycle is counted twice, once in each direction.
